question: Can AnthroSim represent and machine-readably distinguish continuous focal-region residence from bounded repeated temporary aggregation when aggregate focal-region person-days are intentionally kept close?
interpretationBoundary: This benchmark validates AnthroSim M9 software/model capability and observability only. It is not evidence for any real archaeological site or social motive.

continuousResidence.meaning: The deterministic founder households whose persistent synthetic residences lie inside the declared focal region remain there continuously. The only M9 trigger is deliberately outside the 10-year observation window, so no temporary journey occurs.

intermittentAggregation.meaning: The same paired-seed population/world is used. Households resident outside the focal region target nine common annual arrival days, stay 30 days, then return home. Households already resident inside the region remain continuous residents and are ineligible for temporary visits.

classificationRule.capability_distinguished: Every predeclared acceptance condition passes for all paired seeds and the replay/checkpoint checks pass.
classificationRule.near_match_failed: The treatment produces temporary-use structure, but one or more paired seeds exceed the 5% focal person-day matching bound.
classificationRule.not_distinguished: Temporary-use structure is absent or the 25% peak-visitor-share threshold is not met.
classificationRule.degenerate: A paired run does not reach the configured duration, provenance/identity reconciliation fails, or a required derived artifact cannot be regenerated.
